subject: Operator access, KMS locality, and deletion evidence for EU-only processing
messages:
From: Data Protection Officer - HealthCorp <dpo@healthcorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 1 Aug 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Operator access and deletion evidence for EU-only processing

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of HealthCorp's procurement and Schrems II / SCCs review we need a concrete, runnable description of how Redwood ensures EU-only processing for our tenant and how deletion/erasure is proven across primary stores, backups, and operator-facing systems. Specifically we need:

- Confirmation that KMS keys that encrypt customer data at rest are region-bound (where are keys generated/stored?)
- A short runbook or timeline for deletion requests (Purge API -> replicas -> backups -> logs) with expected windows and verifiable artifacts
- A description of operator access controls (breakglass, just-in-time, logging) and any conditions under which data might be accessed outside EU boundaries
- Sample evidence — e.g., a redacted erasure log entry, backup snapshot deletion ID, and a mapping of SCCs scopes applied to the HealthCorp account

We'd like these artifacts by next Friday 2028-08-12 to feed our legal and DPO review. If there are constraints (e.g., longer backup retention in some regions) please call them out and propose mitigations.

Also flag any parts that would require contract language (SCCs addendum, explicit KMS locality warranty).

Best,
Isabel Ruiz
Data Protection Officer
HealthCorp
privacy@healthcorp.com


From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Data Protection Officer - HealthCorp <dpo@healthcorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Aug 2028 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Operator access and deletion evidence for EU-only processing

Hi Isabel,

Thanks — we can provide the artifacts and a short operational runbook. I'm looping in Aditya (infra/ops), Lauren (privacy/legal), and Ben (customer success) to assemble the technical artefacts and the contract language notes.

Attached: healthcorp_sccs_mapping_v1.xlsx (SCCs scope + subprocessor list), eu-deletion-runbook-draft.pdf (initial runbook), sample-erasure-log.txt (redacted).

High-level answers up front:
- KMS locality: Customer data at rest is encrypted with a key material chain anchored to region-specific KMS (EU regions: key material generated and stored within EU KMS). We will provide key metadata and the KMS key-IDs that will be used for HealthCorp.
- Deletion flow: API trigger (customer request) -> immediate mark-for-deletion and KV cache purge -> background async purge from active replicas (within 0–24h, typically seconds for short-lived caches) -> scheduled snapshot/backup tombstone (snapshot retention purge job runs daily; full backup purge within 30 days unless otherwise contractually restricted) -> audit log entry produced for each step.
- Operator access: role-based, time-bound breakglass via privileged sessions; all privileged sessions require ticketing and are recorded and stored in EU logs. Access outside EU is restricted by policy and requires exec approval + documented legal basis.

We expect to have the finalized runbook and a short sample timeline plus a proposed SCCs addendum ready by Friday 2028-08-11. If that's acceptable, we'll follow up with the DocuSign for the attestation.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai


From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Data Protection Officer - HealthCorp <dpo@healthcorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Aug 2028 07:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Operator access and deletion evidence for EU-only processing

Isabel / team —

Following up with the technical specifics you requested (summarised and with example artifacts attached). Quick note: I'm including multi-step timings and a redacted sample erasure log entry at the bottom.

KMS / keys:
- Keys are generated with the cloud provider KMS in the EU region (e.g., eu-west-1). Key IDs (redacted) are: eu-kms-xxxxxxxx. Customer encryption at-rest envelope keys are wrapped by the EU KMS root — key material never leaves the EU.
- Key rotation policy: automatic quarterly rotation; rotation metadata retained in EU.

Backups / snapshot lifecycle:
- Incremental snapshots: every 4 hours; stored in EU object storage when the tenant is configured EU-only.
- Snapshot purge job: tombstones snapshots immediately on request; garbage collection job runs nightly; object deletion may be subject to provider's eventual-deletion window (we provide deletion manifests with object IDs to customers for validation).
- Full backup retention: default 30 days; can be contracted down to 7 days with SLA/commitment.

Operator access controls:
- No standing remote SSH access to data plane. Privileged ops use a bastion with ephemeral certs and recorded sessions (stored in EU log cluster). Breakglass includes: ticket number, approver, timeboxed session, and automated log export attached to a redacted evidence bundle.

Example erasure log (redacted):
- request_id: r-9a7bcd
- tenant: healthcorp
- initiated_by: api:healthcorp:admin
- action_sequence: [marked_for_deletion@2028-08-05T07:12:34Z, purge_replicas@2028-08-05T07:12:40Z, snapshot_tombstone@2028-08-05T07:13:05Z, gc_confirm@2028-08-06T02:05:12Z]
- artifacts: [snapshot_id: sn-0453e, object_ids: [obj-e3f1, obj-a2c8]]

Attachments included: eu-deletion-runbook-draft.pdf, sample-erasure-log.txt. The runbook contains pragmatic checks you can run (curl examples) and the exact endpoints for HealthCorp's tenant.

If HealthCorp legal wants a contractual warranty around KMS locality and a shorter backup window, we can draft SCCs addendum language.

- Aditya
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
